chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Musa ibn Qasim al-Bajali and Abu Qatada Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Hafth, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him: "What is the interpretation of the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'Say: Have you considered if your water should go down, who is it then that will bring you flowing water?'"
He said: "When you lose your Imam and do not see him, what will you do?"

key_terms.تَأْوِيلُ: Interpretation or esoteric meaning of a text
key_terms.غَوْراً: Sunk or submerged (referring to water sources)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the verse 'If your water becomes sunk' in Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: In this tradition from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, the Quranic verse about dry water sources is interpreted as a metaphor for the occultation (Ghayba) of the Imam, where the community faces spiritual deprivation akin to thirst. This exegesis underscores the Shia doctrine that the Imam is the indispensable source of divine guidance and sustenance, and his absence creates a state of existential need for the faithful. It highlights the continuity of spiritual authority even during periods of physical concealment.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 117 - Saad bin Abdullah has narrated from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Isa from Musa bin Qasim Bajali and Abu Qatada Ali bin Muhammad bin Hafas from Ali bin Ja’far from his brother, Musa Ibn Ja’far (a.s) that he said with regard to the verse: “Say: Have you considered if your water should go down, who is it then that will bring you flowing water?”
[67:30] He asked: “What are you going to do when you lose your Imam and don’t see him?”
